## Example 3.3 · The amount charged {#l1-example-3-3 .compact}

```{=html}
<div data-module="quiz" data-correct="1" class="quiz">
<p class="hinge-question">A petrol station records the amount charged to each customer, rounded to the nearest cent. Which statement best describes this random variable?</p>
<div class="choices"><button class="choice" data-answer="1" aria-pressed="false"><b>1</b><span>Discrete, because the charge is rounded and can only take a countable set of values.</span></button><button class="choice" data-answer="2" aria-pressed="false"><b>2</b><span>Discrete, because the amount charged depends on the number of litres purchased.</span></button><button class="choice" data-answer="3" aria-pressed="false"><b>3</b><span>Continuous, because the volume of petrol dispensed can take any value within a range.</span></button><button class="choice" data-answer="4" aria-pressed="false"><b>4</b><span>Continuous, because the amount charged varies between customers.</span></button></div>
<div class="hinge-bottom"><p>Fist on chest. Think quietly. On “show”, hold up 1–4 fingers.</p><button class="reveal-answer primary">Reveal answer</button><button class="reset-question">Reset</button></div>
<div class="hinge-explanation" hidden>1 is the best answer for the final charge recorded in cents. Option 3 describes the volume dispensed, a different variable. Be precise about whether you mean an underlying measurement or the recorded, payable amount.</div>
</div>
```

<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 37 · Example 3.3 · Complete the working in your booklet.</p>

::: notes
Use the same fist-on-chest, simultaneous 1–4 finger response routine as the timed hinges. Screen choices 1–4 correspond to the booklet’s A–D in the same order; question wording and option order are unchanged. Collect responses before using Reveal answer.

Original source label: Mathematics Advanced – HSC Question Bank. Wording retained. The variable as stated is the recorded amount charged in cents, so option 1 is the intended reading. If the intended variable were an unrounded cost calculated from a continuous volume, it could be modelled continuously. Acknowledge this modelling distinction rather than using the question to contradict the running-time example. Option 2 does not establish countability and option 4 is true for both types.
:::
